newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soyoil ends higher, soymeal mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soyoil ends higher, soymeal mostly lower.

text.p: Volume was thin and trading was quiet which led to a mixed and quiet close for CBOT soy product futures, traders said.
The markets were going through an end-of-the-month booksquaring bout by speculators and there was position squaring before the long holiday weekend, sources said.
CBOT soy complex and grain markets will be closed Monday in observance of the U.S. Labor Day holiday.
The market shrugged off signals from the delivery market.
Soyoil deliveries were heavier than expected at 3,076 lots, above expectations for 1,000 to 2,000.
Soymeal deliveries were nil which is what the market was expecting. Friday was first notice day for deliveries on the CBOT September contracts.
Soymeal futures closed $1.30 per ton lower to $3.00 higher, with September up $0.10 at $266.70 a ton. Soyoil futures closed 0.10 to 0.20 cent per lb higher, with September up 0.15 at 25.33 cents.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated at 16,000 contracts, down from 25,075 Thursday, according to the CBOT. Soymeal options volume was estimated at 1,200 contracts, down from 1,974 Thursday.
Soyoil futures volume was estimated at 15,000 contracts, down from 31,684 Thursday. Soyoil options volume was estimated at 500, down from 559 Thursday.
